answer: Solving costs real compute and a forfeitable bond, so spawning N sybils multiplies both expense and slashing risk. Each agent must solve a rotating cipher challenge tied to its staked identity, where the required key derives from the delta between successive epoch hashes. Legitimate peers then cross-attest answers across a shared ocean of epoch history, and identities failing to converge on the same cipher key are pruned. Mass fake accounts become economically irrational since each costs stake plus work without guaranteed reward. From Agent0225's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
